title: The Anxiety-Free Departure
description: Designed specifically for the "Did I leave the stove on?" brain-loop. Capture proof so you can breathe.
goodFor: Capture proof so you can look at your history on the bus and breathe.
steps: Hair Tools: Physically unplug the straighteners or curling iron and move them to a heat-safe surface. (Take a photo)
The Kitchen Hub: Check that every single dial on the stove and oven is pointing to 'Off.' (Take a photo)
The Toaster: Is it unplugged or clear of any crumbs/towels?
Kitchen Sink: Turn the taps tight until there’s no dripping, then check the area for standing water.
Space Heaters: Make sure any portable heaters are unplugged, not just turned off. (Take a photo)
Windows: Walk through every room and physically touch the window latches to ensure they are shut.
The Iron: If you used it, confirm it’s unplugged and standing upright.
Lights: Do a quick sweep of the house and flick off the unnecessary switches.
The Exit: Grab your keys, wallet, and phone. Do you have your bag?
The Final Lock: Lock the front door, turn the handle to test it, and take a photo of the locked deadbolt. (Take a photo)

title: The Deep Sleep Bedtime Scan
description: For when you're in bed and suddenly wonder if the back door is open. Do this once and stay in bed.
goodFor: A comprehensive house check to ensure you can sleep soundly.
steps: Back Door/Patio: Check the sliding door or back latch. Is it fully engaged? (Take a photo)
Ground Floor Windows: Ensure the "forgotten" windows (like the bathroom or laundry room) are snapped shut.
Kitchen Safety: Clear any tea towels away from the stovetop and check the gas/electric is off.
Front Door: Bolt the door and put the chain on.
Pet Check: Does the dog/cat have a full water bowl for the night?
Alarms: Set your house alarm or proximity sensors if you have them.
Phone Charge: Plug your phone in and confirm you see the charging icon.
Coffee Prep: Set the timer or prep the machine so you don't have to think in the morning.
Final Tap Check: Listen for any running water in the bathroom or kitchen.
The "I'm Safe" Moment: Take a photo of your locked front door from the inside so you know you’re secure. (Take a photo)

title: The “Did I take it?” Med Check
description: Perfect for anyone where "autopilot" makes you forget if you actually swallowed the pill.
goodFor: Ensuring strict adherence to medication regimens without second-guessing.
steps: Location: Go to the spot where you keep your medication.
Water: Fill a full glass of water.
The Dose: Count out exactly what you need for right now.
Verification: Hold the pills in your hand and take a quick snap. (Take a photo)
Action: Swallow the medication with the water.
The Bottle: Close the lid tightly (listen for the click).
Refill Check: Do you have enough for tomorrow, or do you need to add "order more" to your list?
The Log: Mark this step as done immediately so the timestamp is accurate.

title: The “No Item Left Behind” Hotel Checkout
description: The ultimate sweep to ensure you don't leave a charger or your passport in a dark drawer.
goodFor: Systematic sweep of hotel rooms to avoid leaving valuables behind.
steps: The Safe: Open it wide and physically feel inside for passports, cash, or jewelry. (Take a photo of the empty safe)
The Shower: Check the ledge for shampoo, rings, or razors.
The "Wall Sweep": Check every single power outlet for phone or laptop chargers.
Under the Bed: Use your phone torch to look for stray socks or shoes that kicked under there.
The Closet: Slide every hanger across to make sure nothing is hiding in the back.
The Nightstand: Open the drawer and check the very back corner.
Towels: Gather used towels into a pile so you can see the floor clearly.
Toiletries: Check the bathroom sink and the medicine cabinet.
The "Big Three": Physically touch your Passport, Wallet, and Phone.
The Key: Take a photo of the room key on the table or as you drop it in the box. (Take a photo)

title: Essential School Morning Run
description: To stop that "I forgot the PE kit" panic 10 minutes into the drive.
goodFor: Morning essentials check to ensure everyone is ready for school.
steps: The Bag: Confirm the main school bag is packed and by the door.
Lunch & Hydration: Is the lunchbox in the bag? Is the water bottle filled and sealed?
The "Extra" Bag: Check the calendar—is it PE day? Swimming? Library book day?
Forms & Folders: Check for any signed permission slips or homework folders.
The Tech: If they use a tablet or laptop for school, is it in the bag and charged?
Weather Check: Do they have a coat or an umbrella if it looks grey outside?
Shoes: Are both shoes found and actually on their feet?
Your Essentials: Do you have your own work bag, keys, and phone?
Pet Exit: If the dog is staying home, is the crate secure or the gate closed?
The Departure: Lock the door and take a photo of the house as you walk away. (Take a photo)

title: The “House Sitter” Handover
description: Evidence that you left the house in a specific state with clear instructions for the sitter.
goodFor: Leaving clear care details and proof of house state for a house sitter.
steps: Emergency Contacts: Leave a note with the vet’s number and your neighbor’s contact. (Take a photo)
Thermostat: Set the heating/cooling to the "away" temperature.
Plants: Give them a final water or group them together for the sitter.
Trash: Empty the kitchen bin so it doesn't smell while you're gone.
The Fridge: Toss out anything that will expire before you get back.
Mail: Tell the sitter where the mailbox key is or where to pile the mail.
Pet Food: Show exactly where the food and bowls are kept. (Take a photo)
Spare Key: Confirm the sitter has their copy and knows how the lock works.
Appliance Check: Unplug non-essential electronics (TVs, blenders, etc.).
The "Final State": Take a wide photo of the living room so you remember how you left it. (Take a photo)

title: Car Security & Parking Peace
description: For that "Did I actually lock the car?" panic. Visual proof that you're secure.
goodFor: Confidence that your car is locked and your spot is remembered.
steps: Windows Up: Do a quick visual check that all windows are fully rolled up.
The Handbrake: Pull it up or engage the electronic brake.
Lights: Ensure the internal lights are off and the headlight dial is set to auto/off.
No Valuables: Make sure no bags or phones are visible on the seats.
The "Look Back": Lock the car using your fob and listen for the "clack" or see the lights flash.
Parking Spot: Take a photo of the car in its spot, making sure a pillar number or a nearby shop is in the frame. (Take a photo)
Keys: Drop your keys into your designated "safe pocket" in your bag or coat.
Personal Items: Check the passenger seat one last time for your sunglasses or water bottle.
The Exit: Head toward the exit with the confidence that you know exactly where you are.

title: The Big Trip Home Shutdown
description: When you’re leaving for a week or more. Prevent a "stale" or "unsafe" house.
goodFor: Peace of mind for long-term absences from the home.
steps: The Fridge Sweep: Throw away the milk and any open perishables that will rot.
Bins: Empty every bin in the house and take the bags outside to the main trash. (Take a photo)
Dishwasher: Run it now or make sure it's empty—don't leave dirty plates for a week.
Water Main: If you usually turn it off, do it now. If not, just double-check the garden hose isn't running.
Thermostat: Set the house to "Away" mode or turn the heating/AC down to a safe minimum.
Electronics: Physically unplug the TV, toaster, and microwave to save energy and prevent surges. (Take a photo)
Plants: Give everyone a big drink or group them together for the person watering them.
Curtains/Blinds: Set them to your preferred "away" position so the house looks occupied but private.
Final Door Check: Lock the back door and any side gates.
The Departure: Take a photo of your keys in your travel bag as you close the front door. (Take a photo)

title: Morning Pet Routine
description: Because "Did I feed the dog?" shouldn't be a source of guilt at your 9 AM meeting.
goodFor: Consistent care for your pets with visual evidence of food and water.
steps: Clean Bowl: Rinse the food bowl so it's fresh for the day.
The Meal: Scoop the food and place it down.
Fresh Water: Empty the water bowl and refill it to the brim. (Take a photo)
Medication: If your pet takes meds, give them now and check the box.
Garden/Toilet: Let them out for a final "bathroom break" before you head out.
Treat/Toy: Leave a "safe" toy or a puzzle treat to keep them occupied.
Gates & Doors: Make sure the "forbidden" rooms (like the nursery or pantry) are snapped shut.
The Goodbye: Check that their collar is on and secure.
The Evidence: Take a photo of the full water bowl and the empty food dish. (Take a photo)

title: The Office/Workspace “Switch-Off”
description: Leave work at work. Transition from "Office Mode" to "Home Mode" without worry.
goodFor: Closing out the workday and ensuring office equipment is safe.
steps: Monitor: Power down your screens.
The "Desk Heater": If you have a space heater under your desk, physically unplug it. (Take a photo)
Sensitive Papers: Clear your desk and put any private documents in a locked drawer.
Personal Items: Do you have your laptop charger, glasses, and keys?
Windows: If you opened a window in your office, make sure it's latched.
Mug Check: Take your coffee mug to the kitchen/breakroom—don't leave it to grow mold!
The "To-Do" List: Write down the very first task for tomorrow morning so you can stop thinking about it.
Lights: Switch off your desk lamp or the main office lights.
The Exit: Lock your office door or pedestal drawer. (Take a photo of the key or the locked door)

title: The Toddler “Survival” Bag
description: Ensures you have the "emergency" items that stop a meltdown.
goodFor: Complete preparation for outings with a toddler.
steps: Nappies/Wipes: Count them out. Do you have at least four?
Spare Outfit: Pack a full change of clothes (including socks!) for the inevitable spill.
Snack Stash: Pack two different types of snacks and a full spill-proof water cup.
The "Safety" Toy: Does the bag have the specific toy or blanket they can't live without? (Take a photo)
Changing Mat: Make sure the portable mat is tucked into the side pocket.
Diaper Disposal: Add a few small plastic bags for "incidents" while you're out.
Seasonal Gear: Sunscreen and a hat, or a warm coat and mittens.
Your Needs: Did you put your keys and wallet in the diaper bag too?
The Buggy: Is the rain cover or sunshade attached?
Ready to Roll: Take a photo of the packed bag sitting by the door. (Take a photo)

title: Gym & Sports Prep
description: Avoid getting to the gym only to realize you forgot your trainers or towel.
goodFor: Ensuring all essential gym gear is packed and ready.
steps: The Shoes: Physically check that your trainers are in the bag.
Fresh Kit: Pack a clean shirt, shorts/leggings, and—critically—fresh socks.
The Towel: Do you have a sweat towel or a shower towel?
Tech & Sound: Are your headphones in the case and charged?
The Lock: Do you have your padlock for the locker? (Take a photo)
Hydration: Fill your water bottle and make sure the lid is on tight.
Gym Pass: Is your membership card or phone app ready?
Post-Workout: Pack a deodorant and any toiletries you need for after the session.
The "Quick Snap": Take a photo of the open bag with the shoes and towel visible. (Take a photo)
